'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Rafah aid distribution killings]]
***At least 103 [[Palestinians]] are killed by [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] fire in the past 24 hours across the [[Gaza Strip]], including 21 people this morning near [[Gaza Humanitarian Foundation]] (GHF) sites, according to the [[Gaza Health Ministry]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/humanitarian-workers-killed-gaza-bus-ambush-that-israel-blames-hamas-2025-06-12/ (Reuters)]
***Eight Palestinian GHF workers are killed and several others are injured after their bus was attacked en route to an [[humanitarian aid|aid distribution]] site in southern [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. The GHF says that [[Hamas]] was responsible. [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/11/world/middleeast/gaza-aid-hamas-attack.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/humanitarian-workers-killed-gaza-bus-ambush-that-israel-blames-hamas-2025-06-12/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)|Israeli invasion of Syria]]
**[[Israel]]i forces kill one person and detain seven people, all [[Syrians]], whom they allege are Hamas members in an early-morning raid on the village of [[Beit Jinn]] in [[Rif Dimashq Governorate]], [[Syria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-israel-hamas-beit-jin-incursion-lebanon-843512c2af36aac7a10f14808cb996d1 (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*Dutch-Israeli writer [[Yael van der Wouden]] wins the 2025 [[Women's Prize for Fiction]] for her novel ''[[The Safekeep]]'', which was also [[short list|shortlisted]] for the [[2024 Booker Prize]]. British [[physician]] and writer [[Rachel Clarke]] wins the sister prize, the [[Women's Prize for Non-Fiction]], for her book about [[palliative care]], ''The Story of a Heart''. [https://apnews.com/article/womens-prize-fiction-nonfiction-winners-6581756b842a58e81d779e725cfae34d (AP)] [https://www.thebookseller.com/news/yael-van-der-wouden-and-rachel-clarke-named-womens-prize-2025-winners (''The Bookseller'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Air India Flight 171]]
**An [[Air India]] [[Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner]] carrying 230 passengers and 12 crew members [[Aviation accidents and incidents|crashes]] into a residential area shortly after [[takeoff]] from [[Ahmedabad Airport]] in [[Gujarat]], [[India]]. Authorities find one survivor from the plane, and 204 bodies have been recovered from the crash site so far. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/air-india-plane-crash-ahmedabad-airport-5177241 (CNA)] [https://www.foxnews.com/world/london-bound-plane-carrying-more-than-200-people-crashes-after-takeoff-india (Fox News)]
*[[2025 South Africa floods]]
**The death toll in the [[flood]]ing caused by heavy rainfall and snowfall from a [[winter storm]] in [[Eastern Cape]], [[South Africa]], increases to 57, with several others still missing. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/rescuers-south-africa-search-missing-after-floods-death-122761587 (ABC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] finds [[Iran]] in breach of its obligations to limit [[uranium]] [[Enriched uranium|enrichment]] and provision of information on its nuclear materials. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ce3v6w2qr12o (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jun/12/un-watchdog-finds-iran-failing-comply-nuclear-obligations (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Disappearance of Annie McCarrick]]
**A man in his 60s is arrested on suspicion of the [[murder]] of Annie McCarrick, who went missing in [[Dublin]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], in 1993. [https://www.rte.ie/news/crime/2025/0612/1518029-annie-mccarrick/ (RTÉ)]
*The [[Internal Security Agency]] of [[Poland]] announce the arrest of a teenager in [[Olsztyn]], [[Warmian–Masurian Voivodeship]], accused with two other men, arrested in April, of planning a [[Far-right politics in Poland|far-right]] [[terrorism in Europe|terrorist]] attack. [https://apnews.com/article/poland-olsztyn-arrest-terrorist-plot-cbc25a9b2eeec1f84cf9d8db7806c734 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Constitutional crisis in Somalia]]
**[[Somalia]]'s [[Federal Government of Somalia|federal government]] calls for the dissolution of the C6+ international coordination framework, saying it is outdated and misrepresents the country’s current political and security progress.  [https://garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/somalia-labels-c6-obsolete-as-opposition-withdraws-from-dialogue (Garowe Online)] [https://chimpreports.com/somalia-declares-c6-framework-obsolete-urges-shift-to-bilateral-engagement/ (ChimpReports)] [https://www.hiiraan.com/news4/2025/Jun/201833/somali_government_calls_for_dissolution_of_c6_framework_citing_obsolescence.aspx (Hiiraan Online)]
*[[June 2025 Los Angeles protests]]
**[[United States Senate|United States senator]] [[Alex Padilla]] of [[California]] is forcibly removed, pushed face-down to the ground, and [[handcuff]]ed after attempting to ask [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|Secretary of Homeland Security]] [[Kristi Noem]] a question at a press conference in [[Los Angeles]]. [https://apnews.com/article/alex-padilla-noem-immigration-protest-california-f67d220a0254473c53c16aa96f554239 (AP)]
*[[Death of Albert Ojwang]]
**[[Kenya Police|Police]] fire [[tear gas]] at demonstrators gathered in [[Nairobi]], [[Kenya]], to protest against the police and its chief, Eliud Lagat, after [[blogger]] Albert Ojwang is confirmed to be killed in custody by the police force, demanding Lagat's [[resignation]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/kenya-police-clash-with-protesters-over-bloggers-death/a-72886994 (DW)]
